subject: containment: Windows drive and UNC paths are paths
prompt:
On Windows the `bash` tool runs through Git Bash, whose `rm` deletes `"C:\Users\<name>\Documents"` exactly as written, and there is no OS sandbox underneath. Auto mode's containment checks never see such a path: the path-candidate matcher (`pathCandidateRe(platform)` in packages/orchestrator/src/auto-containment.ts) finds nothing Windows-shaped even when asked for `"win32"`. On a Windows CI run, a recursive delete of the home's Documents and writes into `.rune/config.toml` and `.rune/memory/entries`, all named with drive paths, went uncaught.

What should happen: `pathCandidateRe("win32")` also yields Windows absolute paths as candidates:
- drive paths with either separator, quoted or bare: `C:\Users\runneradmin\Documents`, `C:/Users/runneradmin/Documents`, mixed `C:\Users\runneradmin/.rune/config.toml`, a lower-case drive (`d:\build`) and a bare drive root (`C:\`);
- UNC paths: `\\server\share\dir`.
A candidate ends where the shell would split the word — whitespace, a quote, a backtick, or a shell operator — so `rm -rf C:\tmp\x && echo done`, `type C:\a\b.txt|more` and `rm -rf C:\tmp\x;ls` yield `C:\tmp\x` and `C:\a\b.txt`. Nothing Windows-shaped may come out of a URL, a time, or a key:value (`https://example.com/a`, `12:30`, `--format=%H:%s`, `a:b`, `-v data:/data`); a drive-relative `C:x` is not a path.

On macOS and Linux nothing changes: the matcher there must stay byte-for-byte the same (`C:\x` is a relative filename on POSIX). Keep the existing exported APIs working, and keep the existing tests passing.
